solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Group of poets knowing Henry the copyist

blocks.note: hep is old slang for well informed, in the know
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
taken as written
one who mimes or mimics is a copyist

explanation.surface: A literary circle of poets includes a clever scribe called Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: HEP + H + THE + MIMER gives HEPHTHEMIMER, a prosody term.
explanation.definitionFit: In classical metre a hephthemimer is a run of seven half-feet, a metrical unit that verse writers use, so loosely a cluster within verse.

clue.text: Iranian official fixes exterior to jet-assisted take-off on hurried flight

indicators.note: being on the exterior means wrapping round the outside of the following abbreviation

blocks.note: to be in a hole, or in holes, is to be in fixes or difficulties
JATO is the standard aviation acronym for jet-assisted take-off
on the lam means in hasty flight, especially from the police

explanation.surface: An Iranian functionary repairs a jet-assisted take-off before a hasty escape.
explanation.walkthrough: HO(JATO)LES + LAM. On the lam is American slang for running away.
explanation.definitionFit: Hojatoleslam is a Shiite clerical title in Iran, ranking just below ayatollah, so the holder is a religious dignitary.

clue.text: Fool set up in charge of lyric poetry

indicators.note: in a down entry, being set up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a dope is a fool
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A foolish person is put in charge of some lyric verse.
explanation.definitionFit: An epode is a kind of lyric poem with alternating long and short lines, so the adjective describes such verse.

clue.text: Where one may see planes turn to starboard shortly?

indicators.note: saying something shortly cuts it short, dropping most of the final word

blocks.note: to hang a right is American slang for turning right, and starboard is the right-hand side

explanation.surface: A question about where aircraft might be spotted when banking right.
explanation.walkthrough: Hang a right, with right cut to its initial R, sounds out HANG A R. Planes look like woodworking tools or flat surfaces, but they are aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangar is the large shed where aircraft are housed and serviced, so planes are seen there.

clue.text: Against importing heroin if in America

indicators.note: importing means bringing something inside, so one word takes the drug abbreviation within it

blocks.note: to can mean against, as in cheek to cheek or close to
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Someone is opposed to smuggling heroin, at least conditionally, in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: T(H)O. 'In America' tells you this is the American spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Tho is the American informal spelling of though, which in the sense even if introduces a concession.

clue.text: Chippy initially has umpteen fried cod perhaps

indicators.note: initially points at the opening letter of each of the next three words

blocks.note: the heads of these three words
cod is one example of a fish

explanation.surface: A fish and chip shop has served a huge amount of fried cod.
explanation.walkthrough: Chippy looks like the British word for a fish and chip shop, which fits the cod; here it means touchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Chippy in British usage means resentful and quick to take offence, much like someone sulky and petulant.

clue.text: Rumor spreading round US city concerning skin disease

indicators.note: a rumour spreading moves about and loses its shape, so its letters are scattered
round means the shuffled letters go about the abbreviation for the city

blocks.note: the American spelling, letters to rearrange
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Gossip is circulating around an American city about a skin complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Morula is an old name for framboesia, or yaws, a tropical infection of the skin, and this adjective relates to it.

clue.text: Like driver’s diversions caught in driving rain?

indicators.note: driving rain is whipped about by the wind, so its letters are blown into a new order
in places the cricket abbreviation inside the rearranged letters

blocks.note: c is the scorecard abbreviation for caught
letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A motorist caught in a downpour needs some distraction on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: Being stuck in a storm is just when a driver wants the radio, so the whole clue paints the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In-car describes things fitted inside a vehicle, such as the entertainment that diverts a motorist.

clue.text: Led by doctor, assembled outside hospital in large numbers

indicators.note: being led by something means having it come first
outside means the gathered word wraps round the hospital abbreviation

blocks.note: MO is a medical officer
banded together means assembled as a group
H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Under a doctor's lead, people gathered around a hospital in crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: MO + BAND(H)ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Mob-handed is British informal usage for turning up as a sizeable gang or crowd, mobbing together.

clue.text: Resembling a draft as William Taft crudely initialled it?

indicators.note: initialled means signed with only the first letters of the name

blocks.note: done crudely is rough
the president's forename
the crude hand applies to the second initial too
the president's surname

explanation.surface: A document resembling a first draft, as signed carelessly by President William Taft.
explanation.walkthrough: Taft initialling crudely writes a rough W and a rough T, so 'crudely' supplies ROUGH before each initial: ROUGH W ROUGH T.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough-wrought means shaped only roughly, at an early unfinished stage, just as a draft is.

clue.text: Fast boat having partly copra hull

indicators.note: having partly means the next words hold a part of the answer within them

blocks.note: found across the two words

explanation.surface: A speedy vessel whose hull is partly made of copra, dried coconut.
explanation.definitionFit: A prahu, or proa, is a Malay sailing craft with an outrigger, known for its speed.

clue.text: Voice disapproval about head primate

indicators.note: about means the jeer goes around the word for head

blocks.note: to boo is to voice disapproval
nob is slang for the head

explanation.surface: Someone jeers at the chief primate, or perhaps a primate bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: BO(NOB)O. Head primate suggests an archbishop, but the primate is an ape.
explanation.definitionFit: The bonobo is an African great ape closely related to the chimpanzee, and apes belong to the primate order.

clue.text: Pease-porridge was revolting start to breakfast earlier

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter
earlier puts that first letter before the verb

blocks.note: the opening letter
rose up in revolt

explanation.surface: The pease-porridge was disgusting at the start of breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' reads as disgusting but means rebelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Brose is a Scottish dish of oatmeal or pease meal stirred with boiling water, a kind of porridge.

clue.text: Fighting heroine, beloved one of Colombian revolutionaries

blocks.note: jo is an old Scots word for a sweetheart
an is the indefinite article, one
o' is the clipped form of of, as in o'clock
the FARC were Colombia's Marxist guerrilla army

explanation.surface: A warrior heroine is the darling of the Colombian rebels.
explanation.walkthrough: JO + AN + O + FARC.
explanation.definitionFit: Joan of Arc led French troops against the English in the Hundred Years War, a famous female warrior saint.

clue.text: An eccentric Australian and English saying

blocks.note: the article
in Australian slang a dag is an eccentric or amusing character
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An oddball from Australia and an Englishman share a saying.
explanation.definitionFit: An adage is a proverb, a traditional maxim expressing common wisdom.

clue.text: Webern, possibly not one turning up key material using offcuts

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the words are read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: not plus a, one
A is a musical key
list is the selvage of cloth, and also fabric made from such strips

explanation.surface: Webern perhaps wasn't one to dig out key material from discarded scraps.
explanation.walkthrough: NOT A turned up gives A TON, then A + LIST. Key material sounds musical, but the key is just A.
explanation.definitionFit: Anton Webern, of the Second Viennese School, composed music without a tonal centre, so he is an example of such a composer.

clue.text: Shellfish two pints a shilling once?

blocks.note: a quart is two pints, abbreviated qu.
taken as written
hog was old slang for a shilling, the pre-decimal British coin

explanation.surface: A price list from long ago: shellfish at two pints for a shilling.
explanation.definitionFit: The quahog is a thick-shelled edible clam of the North American Atlantic coast, a bivalve mollusc.

clue.text: At least three birds, one that was flightless

blocks.note: no letters: this counts the birds, one plus a plural of two or more
one small songbird
the ani is a black tropical American cuckoo, here in the plural, so at least two more

explanation.surface: Of a few birds counted, one was unable to fly.
explanation.walkthrough: TIT + ANIS: one bird plus a plural of another must be at least three. The ani is a black American cuckoo.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanis was a giant prehistoric terror bird of the Americas, too heavy to take to the air.

clue.text: Old spear has to be modified

indicators.note: to be modified means the letters are to be altered into a fresh order

blocks.note: letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An ancient lance needs some modification.
explanation.definitionFit: Spears were once shafted with ash timber, so the tree's name came to stand for the weapon in old poetry.

clue.text: Queen supporting outrageous Ascot society hats

indicators.note: something outrageous is wild and out of order, so the letters go astray
in a down entry, supporting puts the royal letter underneath the rearranged letters

blocks.note: letters to rearrange
R for regina, queen
S is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: The Queen shows approval of the extravagant headwear at Royal Ascot.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Ascot is a fashionable English race meeting famous for outlandish hats.
explanation.definitionFit: A castor is an old word for a hat, originally one made of beaver fur, castor being Latin for beaver.

clue.text: Give girl run around right up to date?

indicators.note: running around something means encircling it, so one word goes around the name

blocks.note: to spew is to give out or emit
a girl's name

explanation.surface: Hand a young woman a run round the very latest course?
explanation.walkthrough: SP(ANN)EW.
explanation.definitionFit: Span-new is a dialect form of brand-new, meaning absolutely fresh and current.

clue.text: Every year see a stupid American jock?

blocks.note: p.a. is per annum, every year
to look is to see
taken as written

explanation.surface: Each year you meet a dim American sporty type.
explanation.definitionFit: Palooka is American slang for a clumsy, slow-witted person, especially a second-rate boxer or athlete.

clue.text: Reptilian language — that’s surprising

definitions.note: used as a noun, a reptile

blocks.note: lang. is the abbreviation for language
aha is the exclamation of surprised discovery

explanation.surface: Someone is startled to find a language that belongs to snakes and lizards.
explanation.definitionFit: The langaha is a Madagascan tree snake with a strange leaf-like snout, and snakes are reptiles.

clue.text: Sunak put out what could be annoying bull

indicators.note: being put out means disturbed and displaced, so the letters are knocked into another order

blocks.note: the surname of the former British prime minister, letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Rishi Sunak was irritated by something that might be talking nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: Bull suggests nonsense, but it is a bull elephant being prodded.
explanation.definitionFit: An ankus is the hooked goad used by Indian mahouts to drive elephants, so it might well irritate a bull elephant.

clue.text: Spaghetti hoops coming with canellini?

indicators.note: coming with means arriving inside the following word, carried along within it

blocks.note: found within the word

explanation.surface: Tinned pasta rings served alongside some white beans.
explanation.walkthrough: The bean is usually spelt cannellini; the setter's single n makes the hidden letters fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Anelli is Italian for little rings, the small pasta loops sold in tins in tomato sauce.

clue.text: Aphrodite, universal queen over Athens, primarily

indicators.note: in a down entry, over places the queen above the next letter
primarily means taking only the first letter

blocks.note: U is the film classification for universal
a rani is an Indian queen
the city's opening letter

explanation.surface: The goddess of love reigns over Athens as universal queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Urania, meaning heavenly, is an epithet of Aphrodite in her role as goddess of spiritual love.

clue.text: Girl, one back in Scotland …

indicators.note: going back means the word is read from right to left

blocks.note: ane is the Scots word for one
no letters: this marks the word for one as Scots dialect

explanation.surface: A lass, one returning home to Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Ena is a female forename, so any girl so called fits.

clue.text: Sectarian gathering about a book

indicators.note: about means the gathering goes round the article and the book abbreviation

blocks.note: a bee is a social gathering for work, as in a quilting bee
taken as written
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A religious sect meets to discuss a book.
explanation.walkthrough: B(A + B)EE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Babee is a follower of the Bab, founder of the Persian Babi sect, so a member of that faith group.

clue.text: … or she will go back, one used to plain living

indicators.note: to go back is to run in the opposite direction, so the words are read right to left

blocks.note: taken as written
she is the girl of the previous clue, joined by the ellipsis
'll is the contracted will

explanation.surface: A woman returns home, being accustomed to a simple life.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to 26: she is ENA. Plain living suggests frugality, but it means living on the plains.
explanation.definitionFit: A llanero is a cowboy or inhabitant of the llanos, the vast grassy plains of Venezuela and Colombia.

clue.text: Kirkpatrick’s invested in awful stale Edinburgh rock

indicators.note: the possessive asks for the surname's own initial letter
something awful is in a dreadful state, so the letters are jumbled
invested in means placed inside the jumbled word

blocks.note: the initial
letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Kirkpatrick has put money into some unpleasantly stale Edinburgh rock.
explanation.walkthrough: Edinburgh rock is a crumbly Scottish sweet, but here it is a Scots word for a kind of stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Sklate is the Scots form of slate, a rock, so Edinburgh marks it as Scottish usage.

clue.text: What could knock Maude into shape?

definitions.text: What could knock Maude into shape?

indicators.note: knocking something about bashes it out of its existing form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a woman's name, letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone asks what fitness regime would get a woman called Maude in trim.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the instruction to rearrange the name and the meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Medau is a German system of rhythmic gymnastic exercise with balls and hoops, a way to get physically fit.

clue.text: Money of old Greek seen in fancy jewellery acting corruptly

indicators.note: seen in means the coin appears inside the jewellery word

blocks.note: bling is flashy jewellery
the obol was a small coin of ancient Greece

explanation.surface: Ancient Greek coins turn up in showy jewellery from a crooked dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: B(OBOL)LING.
explanation.definitionFit: Bobol is West Indian slang for fraud or graft, so bobolling means engaging in dishonest dealing.

clue.text: Trumpet section’s leaving legato effect

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so that abbreviation is taken away

blocks.note: a slur is the curved mark binding notes smoothly
S is the abbreviation for section

explanation.surface: The brass section is leaving out the smooth legato playing.
explanation.definitionFit: A lur is a long curved Bronze Age horn from Scandinavia, an ancient brass instrument.

clue.text: Vindicate biographer of King Alfred’s time

blocks.note: Asser was the Welsh monk who wrote the life of Alfred the Great
t is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Justify a claim made in the era of King Alfred's biographer.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert can mean to defend or uphold a claim or right, which is to justify it.

clue.text: I mostly flounder in some regions over Indian food

indicators.note: mostly means almost all of the word, dropping its last letter
turned over, the letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: taken as written
fluke is a dialect name for the flounder

explanation.surface: Someone mostly struggles, in some places, over Indian cuisine.
explanation.walkthrough: Flounder looks like a verb meaning struggle; it is the flatfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Kulfi is a dense Indian ice cream, often flavoured with cardamom or pistachio, a South Asian dessert.

clue.text: Situate farms subject to changing Turkish local jurisdiction

indicators.note: being subject to changing means the letters are to be put into another order

blocks.note: letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Locate farms whose administration falls under shifting Turkish rule.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutessarifat was an administrative district of the Ottoman Empire governed by a mutessarif, a provincial governor.
